text:
Jordan: Heads-up — I'm about to land a refactor that prunes unused module dependencies and moves several internal modules from git urls -> registry modules. It'll also update the .terraform.lock.hcl partially (only modules that changed). Asking for a quick pass: any concerns about provider version pinning or secret path wiring?
Lexi: quick q — are we hoisting provider blocks to root or keeping per-module providers? I know some modules expect explicit provider aliasing.
Jordan: hoisting to root for the shared infra modules (network, rds) and adding provider_alias where modules actually need different regions/accounts. plan shows most modules will inherit.
Mike: my main worry is lockfile churn. If you're only regenerating subset, make sure CI run does `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64` for the full graph afterwards. Otherwise downstream workspaces may diverge.
Jordan: yes, I ran `terraform providers lock` locally for the repo but not for every platform. I can add a CI job. Also planning to split the provider pin from the module source change in separate commits so rollback is easier.
Irina: on secrets wiring — any state moves? e.g., we previously had modules writing secrets at path `secret/data/app/<env>/db` and some modules reference `data.external` helper that expects the legacy path.
Jordan: good catch. There is one state rename: modules/db -> modules/rds_shared; I added `terraform state mv module.db module.rds_shared` in the migration plan and a note to ops. No secrets path rename, just module namespace change.
Lexi: for safety add a `locals { legacy_secret_prefix = "secret/data/app" }` temporarily and keep the data lookup compatible. Then remove in a followup once everything is stable.
Mike: CI-bot: can you post the plan link? need to eyeball resources that will be replaced vs recreated.
ci-bot: CI plan uploaded: https://ci.redwood-infer.example/plan/1254 (public to team). Summary: 3 resources to be replaced, 1 to be moved, 0 destroy.
Jordan: plan excerpt:
```
-/+ aws_db_instance.main (new resource required)
~ resource "aws_ssm_parameter" "db_password" {
    ~ name = "/redwood/db/password" -> "/redwood/db/password" # forces replacement due to module address change
}
```
Lexi: replacement for db password param is scary. Is that because of module address? If so we should import the existing SSM param into new module state instead of replacing.
Jordan: yep it's module address causing replace. I'll add `terraform state mv` for the parameter resource as well:
```
terraform state mv module.db.aws_ssm_parameter.db_password module.rds_shared.aws_ssm_parameter.db_password
```
Irina: also confirm KMS key usage — if the param is encrypted with a CMK, moving without updating the key reference should be fine, but double-check access policy for the new IAM role used by rds_shared.
Mike: run `terraform plan -replace=module.db.aws_ssm_parameter.db_password` in CI to test the move? might be flaky.
Jordan: I'll add a gated run in staging: deploy plan -> run state mv -> apply. Then run production apply only after manual signoff.
terraform-bot: Reminder: when moving state between modules, ensure backup of state file and lock; `terraform state pull > backup.tfstate` recommended.
Lexi: tiny nit — update the module README to mention registry source (registry.redwood.example/infra/network) and bump CHANGELOG. Helps infra teams track changes.
Jordan: will do. Also adding a brief migration note in the PR description with the exact `state mv` commands and the CI plan link.
Mike: LGTM from infra side. if you can add the full lock regen in CI and the state mv steps in a migration script, I'm happy to approve.
Jordan: thanks all — I'll push the first commit (module source swap) and ping again after the CI plan completes. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: Build 1254 succeeded, plan created at https://ci.redwood-infer.example/plan/1254 (same link)
Irina: thanks — once Jordan posts the migration script I'll run the staging apply and confirm DB param didn't get recreated.
Jordan: noted — I'll include `--state` backup and step-by-step apply notes. ETA for PR: ~2h.
Mike: quick reminder — if any team needs to lock specific provider versions for compatibility, add a `required_providers` block at root with explicit versions, e.g., `aws = { version = ">= 4.0, < 5.0" }`.
Jordan: copied. will include provider pin in separate commit as discussed. pinging when ready.
